text: **dsh-web-file-uploader**（DSH 网页插件）：为 DSH 网页聊天输入框添加回形针附件入口，并在发送时把所选文件交给模型读取。它通过浏览器上传路由和 DSH 主机文件服务保存附件，在用户消息发送前注入文件路径；图片会根据模型能力以原生图片附件或路径文本处理。主要功能包括多文件选择、上传进度与附件卡片、内容去重、上传文件管理和桌面本地文件引用。适合需要在 DSH 对话中附加文档或图片的网页及桌面用户。无需 API Key；需使用 DSH web profile。

**dsh-web-file-uploader** (DSH web plugin): Adds a paperclip file picker to DSH chat. Uploads selected files to host storage and attaches paths or native images to messages. Includes progress, deduplication, file management, and Desktop local-file references. No API key required.

**dsh-web-file-uploader** 的功能「多文件上传」：在聊天输入框打开文件选择器并显示附件卡片与进度。选择文件后流式上传到 DSH 主机，发送后由插件把附件交给对话处理。
**dsh-web-file-uploader** 的功能「发送时注入附件」：发送用户消息时将仍打开的附件路径加入消息；支持的图片还可作为原生图片附件传入模型。
**dsh-web-file-uploader** 的功能「内容去重」：上传前计算文件哈希并查询主机索引。若已有相同内容，插件复用已存路径并登记会话引用。
**dsh-web-file-uploader** 的功能「管理已上传文件」：设置页列出插件登记的文件并提供选择删除；会话仍引用的文件会显示为使用中。
**dsh-web-file-uploader** 的功能「桌面本地文件引用」：桌面选择文件后可登记原始路径供会话使用，不传输文件字节；移除卡片只取消引用。

dsh-web-file-uploader README · dsh-web-file-uploader：This is a file-upload plugin developed for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It adds a [DeepSeek Web Chat](https://chat.deepseek.com) style **paperclip attach button** to the prompt input field, uploads the selected files to the **DSH host machine**, and applies **model-aware adaptation** so the files are actually readable by the running model; it also supports **content-addressed deduplication**.

dsh-web-file-uploader README · dsh-web-file-uploader：It currently supports web and desktop; support for [dsh-TUI](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI) is planned.

If you want to see the plugin's running effects, see in [Gallary](GALLARY.md).

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Features：- 📎 Paperclip button in the composer tool row: its style basically matches the button inside DeepSeek Web Chat, with the paperclip rotated 45° to distinguish it from the official built-in feature.
- The official upload entry can be **replaced**: the shell's "Add → File" row (shared by the `+` menu and the `/` slash menu) is swapped in place for this plugin's own entry — same "File" text, but the icon uses this plugin's own angled paperclip and the command becomes `attach-file`. The standalone composer button stays visible by default and can be hidden while the replacement is on, letting the menu entry be the only upload control.
- Multi-file selection; each file is shown as a **preview-style attachment card** above the composer (images show a thumbnail): reading → uploading → saved, with copy-path and remove actions, plus a permanent delete button that appears only when a new stored copy was created (that action really deletes the file from disk).
- Once a real upload creates a new copy, it is stored on the DSH host in a directory managed by the plugin, and collected automatically by GC (garbage collection).
- Filenames are sanitized automati

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Usage：> This assumes you have just installed the plugin and have not changed any default setting. The plugin's settings page documents every option in detail if you want to look into them.

Click the angled paperclip button in the prompt input field and the system file picker opens; choose the files you need and confirm.

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Usage：After uploading, each file is shown as a card above the prompt input field where you can adjust it. Once you press send, the cards still present are turned into file paths and injected into the text prompt, appended to the end of the user message for the model to read and analyse. Read on for more technical details.

To install this plugin right away, jump to [Installation](#installation).

dsh-web-file-uploader README · File storage location：An uploaded file copy lands in `$DSH_HOME/uploads` (default `~/.dsh/uploads`) on the DSH host.

The deduplication index (`uploads/.dfu-index.json`) lives in the same directory as the stored files.

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Model-aware adaptation & the attachment-card design：Uploaded files are shown as **attachment cards** in the dock above the composer. The cards are the source of truth for injection:

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Model-aware adaptation & the attachment-card design：| State | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Card present | The file's absolute path is injected into **the user messages about to be sent**. |
| Card closed (`×`) | The file card disappears, and the uploaded copy is **kept on disk** and tracked by the plugin. |
| Card deleted (🗑) | The file card disappears, the uploaded copy is **permanently removed from the DSH host**, and the tracking index is updated accordingly. |
| Ctrl+V paste | Pasted images ride the native draft pipeline; the plugin does not interfere |

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Model-aware adaptation & the attachment-card design：The distinction between `×` and 🗑 is intentional: `×` just stops injecting (you might want the model to find the file later), while 🗑 is a statement that you are **done with the file forever**. When the last reference is deleted, the file is removed from disk if it lives in the plugin-managed directory; if another live session still references the same deduplicated copy, the file is kept and only this session's reference is dropped.

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Model-aware adaptation & the attachment-card design：A re-upload hits deduplication and reuses the same stored path, so such a card merely **borrows** an existing copy rather than owning it. Those cards do not show 🗑, because deleting permanently from here would also remove a file other references still use, so they keep only `×` to release the reference; for file-level deletion use the plugin's settings page, where the "in use" rule also protects files referenced by live sessions.

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Model-aware adaptation & the attachment-card design：This is a deliberate design decision: a card **does not disappear automatically** after sending (unlike paste previews that clear on send), so you decide how long a file stays "attached" to the conversation. Each injection is one-shot (one per message), and the injected block lists exactly the files of all currently **open** cards.

Injection is distinguished by model capability:

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Model-aware adaptation & the attachment-card design：| Model type | Image files (png/jpeg/webp/gif) | Other files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Multimodal** (reported `inputModalities` includes `image`) | Native `ImageBlock` via the attachments service, the image becomes part of the request like a normal attachment, with **no extra prompt text** | Path text block |
| **Text-only** (e.g. DeepSeek V4 series) | Path text block (the model can still call vision tools to parse it) | Path text block |

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Model-aware adaptation & the attachment-card design：Note that if you also want an image to reach a natively image-capable model as a plain text path instead, so the model can process it beforehand and then read it, turn on the "Images bypass the native pipeline" option in the plugin's settings page and save.

The capability check uses `llm.resolveModelInfo().inputModalities` (cached for 10 minutes, safe text-only fallback).

The injected prompt uses a readable, **English-only format for the model to read**:

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Model-aware adaptation & the attachment-card design：```plaintext
-----
[Attached files] Some files have been uploaded with this message:
- /path/to/file1.txt
- /path/to/image1.png

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Compatibility with vision-tools and other plugins：- **Zero coupling**: the plugin only injects absolute paths into the prompt; it never calls, wraps, or assumes any auxiliary tool, and a tool such as vision-tools or a similar image-reading tool simply works independently once it has the path.
- **Native multimodal path**: for image-capable models, images are injected as native `ImageBlock`s, and the model can read and recognise them with its own multimodal ability.
- **Non-invasive**: injection targets only real user messages; steering / system messages are never injected, and a message that already carries the `[Attached files]` marker is never injected twice. Pasting images via Ctrl+V is handled entirely by the product's native pipeline.

text: dsh-web-file-uploader README · Local directory (development; run `pnpm build` in it first, and replace `/path/to` with the actual relative or absolute path)：The repository ships **sources only**: `lib/` and `client/src/client.js` are git-ignored build output, generated by `pnpm build` (and by the `prepare` script when a package is installed from git). A plain checkout has no bundle until it is built, so use the release tarball (or npm) for a ready-to-install package, or allow pnpm to run the `prepare` script for git installs. A tarball URL is pinned in the profile: switching releases means `remove` + `add` the new URL.

dsh-web-file-uploader README · Development status：- ✅ Static bundle: card-driven injection, model-aware adaptation, dedup, i18n UI, settings panel with batch delete, and the replaceable add/slash-menu entry — all covered by the test suites
- ✅ Distribution: each bare-version tag runs CI, builds the bundle and attaches the installable tarball to the GitHub Release (no build needed to install)
- ⚠️ The client build wrapper in `scripts/build.ts` is a best-effort emulation of the DSH web toolchain output; verify it against the real web build before distributing (compare with a shipped `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-*` `lib/client.js`)
